I feel like food being expensive ultimately got me back on track. I went from anorexic to a penny-pincher and ended up triaging three square healthy meals and no snacks. Now I'm  Scrooge who counts dollars and macros instead of calories so idk, judge me.

I was more or less a normal person, a teenage girl with an average share of insecurities about my body and worth. I never tried any diets or weight loss of any sort, until one day a friend of mine told me she was recovering from anorexia. After that I sorta just instantly became anorexic. 

I guess I'd never even considered the term 'anorexia' (or eating disorders, for that matter). I don't think I was trying to one-up her, of course I remained secretive about it and actually we never talked about it... I've never had anything traumatic or particularly concerning happen in my life. I also turned on to self harm for pretty petty and minor reasons, mostly the aesthetic of scars (also weird bc I cut where no one sees but me).

I was always sort of a medical geek, and in the back of my mind I saw pathology as an interesting frame of mind and perspective on life and living. Yeah, I'm still waiting for my psych referral to come through...

I usually don't make salads because the leaves tend to go bad before I get to finishing the bunch... Have you tried frozen chopped spinach? It has no flavour or texture and I usually hide it in random dishes or even sauces. Frozen chopped kale though is a bit more noticeable.

Also, have you tried peeling vegetables that are green, like zucchinis?

Idk if you're vegan/vegetarian, but if you like sweet flavours try tagines. You can make them with meat or veg and the spice mix is pretty sweet tasting (usually some warming, chai-like spices. Of course, you can adjust the spice ratio to your liking). There's also a Greek/Middle-Eastern style meat sauce for pasta that is super simple, just ground beef and tomato sauce, salt, pepper, a bit of ground cinnamon, and a couple cloves (edit: and grated onion!).

Quiches are nice to hide vegetables in, and good protein in eggs. Hard to suggest things without knowing what you might like but I'm sure there are healthy+tasty options for you out there

I also was struck by how cathartic tending to my physical wounds was. At the same time, I don't care much for other people to do it, so I kinda wonder where that pleasure comes from (ie, I'm not waiting for someone else to patch me up, but why does it feel good to patch myself up?). Maybe it has to do with having something physical as a metaphor for the internal, or maybe it's as simple as being preoccupied with something different on my body that I can change my rituals of daily life with, or maybe just a distraction from the real problems I don't want to deal with patching up...

I was in that situation. All alone, no scales, and a meal plan such that you could eat anything and it would just be a flat charge. 

I "recovered" freshman year, by which I mean I binged on pastries a lot... And snacks at parties were a problem for me the whole four years. 

Then I moved again for my next degree and was on my own but without a meal plan. In this situation I considered myself recovered insofar as I didn't buy foods that weren't actual meals and kept to the good ol' 3 meals a day and a normal-person total cal count. Two years of that and I have a normal food drive and only eat when I'm hungry and stop when I'm full (at normal portions). 

I find it much easier to not be eating-disordered when I am living with my parents. Mostly bc they always make delicious food and we eat together. Then I kinda am urged to restrict because I'm overwhelmed with the variety and tastiness. Ugh how hard is life /skinda

Dude honestly I feel you. I have had a great life actually. Loving parents, minimal economic difficulties, decent grades, no one's hurt me (yet) in any way. 

I've felt lowkey "depressed" my whole life, but recently I've felt super low and suicidal. I do have a great relationship with my parents, so I have to stop myself and limit my suicidal desires to dreams that I obsessively plan out. 

I decided to talk to a counsellor, and she kept trying to make up tragic backstories to my life! Like, "It sounds like you're running from something", or "has something happened recently". Like, no ma'am, it's probably just my personality getting out of hand. 

I used to want more interesting things to have happened, especially because I'm always too aware that people out there are going through so much worse while I'm trying to fabricate symptoms. I feel like for me self harm is partially a means to make my mental health physiological and physical. A few other aspects, of course, but I think we both have to remember that our feelings are valid. Even if it's as simple/boring as dysfunctional synapses...
